items.headline: Houthi strikes hit Saudi airports and oil sites
items.summary: Houthi rebels struck Saudi airports, killing three people and wounding dozens, as Yemen's war escalates. Earlier strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure are adding to regional tension and pushing oil prices up.

items.headline: Russian strike on a Ukrainian bus kills 30
items.summary: Russian attacks in eastern Ukraine, including a strike on a public bus, killed 30 people, while power outages in Kyiv are getting worse.

items.headline: South Korea recalls its ambassador to Ukraine and tests a hypersonic weapon
items.summary: Seoul is pulling its ambassador from Kyiv over a dispute about North Korean prisoners of war. Separately, South Korea flight-tested its first homegrown hypersonic weapon after a North Korean hypersonic launch and mine blasts that wounded three South Korean soldiers.

items.headline: Isaias becomes a hurricane as the Gulf Coast prepares
items.summary: Isaias has strengthened into a hurricane, and Gulf Coast residents are preparing for storms. Forecasters had said a week ago that the Atlantic might go the whole season without a hurricane.

items.headline: Midterms: about 60 House seats will decide control, and Kansas is now a Senate battleground
items.summary: Both parties are concentrating money on roughly 60 House districts that Trump carried by about nine points on average in 2024. In Kansas, Republican Sen. Roger Marshall faces a tightening race against Democrat Adam Hamilton.

items.headline: Trump's $90 Medicare rebate rolls out, but millions don't qualify
items.summary: The administration is sending one-time $90 payments toward Medicare Part B premiums at an estimated cost of $2 billion. Many enrollees aren't eligible, and critics call it a political stunt ahead of the midterms.

items.headline: ICE quietly used a New Jersey warehouse as a detention site, neighbors say
items.summary: An NPR investigation examines local accounts that ICE ran a detention facility out of a warehouse in Roxbury, New Jersey, over the summer. The report raises questions about oversight of temporary detention sites.

items.headline: A $110 billion Skydance deal for Warner Bros. Discovery
items.summary: The Ellison family's proposed purchase of Warner Bros. Discovery, owner of CNN and the Warner studio, would concentrate control over major news and entertainment outlets. Critics argue it would leave less room for dissent.

items.headline: Syrian general accused of atrocities shielded in Lebanon, NPR and BBC find
items.summary: A joint NPR and BBC investigation found that a former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity lives in Lebanon. The report says he has been financed and protected by U.S. and Lebanese authorities.

items.headline: French students invoke May 1968 in school-funding protests
items.summary: Students protesting underfunded schools in France are carrying signs that reference the 1968 uprising that nearly brought down the government. More than 250,000 people have marched over education reforms, class sizes and building conditions.

digest.overview:
At home, Isaias became the Atlantic season's first hurricane and is heading toward eastern Louisiana and the western Florida Panhandle. Both parties are pouring money into about 60 competitive House districts, and Kansas has become an unexpected Senate battleground. Trump rallied in San Antonio for Texas Senate nominee Ken Paxton, who has trailed Democrat James Talarico in nearly every poll. The administration's one-time $90 Medicare rebate is rolling out, though millions of enrollees don't qualify. The EPA said it will further loosen methane limits for oil and gas operations. NPR reports ICE quietly detained people in a New Jersey warehouse this summer. Actor Eva Marie Saint died at 102.

Abroad, Houthi strikes on Saudi airports killed three and injured 36, and more than 200,000 Yemenis have been displaced by recent fighting. Projectiles hit a tanker north of Qatar after Iranian warnings over its Strait of Hormuz blockade, and oil prices rose more than 2%. In Ukraine, Russian attacks including a strike on a public bus killed 30 people as blackouts deepen in Kyiv. South Korea will recall its ambassador to Ukraine over a dispute about North Korean prisoners of war, and it test-flew its first homegrown hypersonic weapon after a North Korean launch. Russia denied reports of a second pneumonic plague case tied to an Irkutsk lab, where about 200 people were quarantined. Spain will hold a snap election on November 29 amid a housing crisis, and French students staged new mass protests over crowded schools. Indonesia is restricting access to forest data as deforestation surges.

home.overview:
The White Sox can clinch a trip to the ALCS tonight, leading Cleveland 2–1 in their ALDS with Game 4 in Chicago after the Guardians stayed alive with a 9–3 win; the winner meets Tampa Bay, which swept the Yankees. The NLCS is set: the Dodgers closed out Atlanta 4–1 and the Brewers ousted San Diego 3–1, with Game 1 in Milwaukee on Sunday. In the NFL, the winless Buccaneers visit Dallas on Thursday night with rookie Jalon Daniels at quarterback, and Sunday opens with Eagles vs. Jaguars in London. The Chiefs, 49ers and Vikings remain unbeaten, while Lamar Jackson and Ja'Marr Chase are uncertain. The NBA tips off Oct. 20 with Celtics at Pistons.

Club soccer returns this weekend, led by Liverpool vs. Man City on Sunday, with City perfect at 5–0 atop the Premier League. Barcelona are 7–0 in La Liga and Dortmund lead the Bundesliga. During the break, England beat Croatia 7–0, the USA edged Canada 1–0 and South Korea beat Uzbekistan 2–0, while Lionel Messi played his last game for Argentina. The Champions League resumes Oct. 13–14 with Man City vs. PSG. In K League 1, FC Seoul lead by 15 points and host Jeju SK on Saturday.

brief: Tonight: Guardians at White Sox in ALDS Game 4 (8 p.m. ET, TBS). Chicago leads 2–1, and the winner meets Tampa Bay in the ALCS starting Monday, Oct. 12.
Cleveland stayed alive with a 9–3 Game 3 win. José Ramírez went 2-for-4 with a double, a triple and two RBI.
The Dodgers closed out Atlanta 4–1 in NLDS Game 4. Andy Pages broke it open with a bases-loaded, two-run single in the seventh.
Milwaukee eliminated San Diego 3–1 in Game 4. Garrett Mitchell had a triple and an RBI single, and he robbed Manny Machado of a potential game-tying homer.
The Rays swept the Yankees, taking Game 3 4–3 in the Bronx behind Victor Mesa Jr.'s two-run homer off Max Fried.
The NLCS (Dodgers vs. Brewers) opens Sunday, Oct. 11, in Milwaukee. Start times haven't been announced.
